title: Long-tail prompt cluster cache econ breakdown
content:
Purpose:
This sheet models the unit economics and monthly savings for an alternative approach to prefix/KV caching that clusters long-tail prompts into canonical prefix groups before caching. The goal is to estimate how much headroom exists for cost savings (USD) and p95 latency impact across realistic customer distributions where ~70% of traffic is head prompts and ~30% is a long tail of low-frequency prompts.

Executive summary (short):
- Clustering long-tail prompts into 10–100 canonical groups can increase effective hit rate on the KV/prefix cache for the long tail from ~3–7% up to 18–35% depending on cluster granularity and sequence-length variance.
- For a mid-sized customer with 350M tokens/mo, modeled monthly GPU inference spend reduction ranges from $6.5k to $27k (2%–8% reduction) under conservative assumptions, and up to $40k (12% reduction) in optimistic batching + cluster reuse scenarios.
- p95 latency impact is neutral-to-positive when clustering reduces repeated attention work; in worst-case additional prefetch overhead increases p95 by ~30–60ms.
- Recommendation: run an A/B probe implementing offline clustering + simulated cache in front of production for 4 weeks, coupled with a small on-host prefetcher and a TTL-based demotion policy.

Assumptions (base case):
- Baseline customer: 350M tokens/month, 450k requests, avg tokens/request = 777 (mixed long sequence workload), baseline KV/prefix cache hit rate = 12% overall (head 40% requests have 55% hit within head patterns; long tail 60% requests have 3% hit).
- Cost model: $X per token served on GPU: use normalized unit costs where baseline inference compute = $0.000012 per token (post-quantization, amortized infra). Embedding/indexing and storage costs are accounted separately at $0.7k/mo.
- Cache refresh cost: clustering recompute and index maintenance costs assigned as (+$1.2k/mo) in conservative case, or (+$3.2k/mo) in aggressive prefetch case (CPU + small NVMe ops).
- Prefetch window: prefetch up to first 32 tokens of clustered canonical prefix when cluster confidence >= threshold (tunable).

Scenario table (simulated outputs):
Columns: scenario_id | cluster_count | long_tail_effective_hitrate | overall_hitrate | monthly_savings_usd | pct_cost_reduction | added_ops_cost_usd | net_monthly_savings_usd | p95_latency_delta_ms
Data rows (rounded):
S1 | 10 clusters (coarse)  | 18% | 18% overall | $6,500 | 2.1% | $1,200 | $5,300 | +45ms
S2 | 25 clusters (balanced) | 24% | 17.5% overall | $12,800 | 4.1% | $1,800 | $11,000 | +30ms
S3 | 50 clusters (fine)     | 29% | 18.8% overall | $19,200 | 6.1% | $2,600 | $16,600 | +20ms
S4 | 100 clusters (very fine) | 35% | 20.4% overall | $27,600 | 8.8% | $3,200 | $24,400 | +15ms
S5 | 50 clusters + batching opt | 34% | 21.1% overall | $40,100 | 12.1% | $3,400 | $36,700 | -12ms (improved p95 via reduced compute)

Notes on numbers:
- "overall_hitrate" mixes head traffic (unchanged) and adjusted long-tail effective hit-rate from clustering.
- Monthly savings derived from token-level cost delta after accounting for reduced GPU per-token compute due to cache hits (assumes 60% cost reduction per token hit).
- Added ops cost includes clustering retrain schedule (daily mini-batches), metadata write IOPS, and prefetch CPU cycles.

Sensitivity analysis (quick):
- If baseline long-tail volume is higher (40% vs 30%) savings scale roughly linearly to long-tail fraction.
- If prefetching increases storage egress by >15% it erodes savings and can flip net_savings negative for S1; larger cluster counts are more robust to egress inflation.
- Model sequence-length variance: customers with median seq_len < 200 show smaller absolute savings (less prefix work), but relative pct improvement often increases because shorter sequences are more cacheable.

Operational design considerations: 
1) Cluster lifecycle: weekly reclustering + hotlist for ephemeral new prompts. Clusters have a TTL and are validated by a measured reuse score before write-back to KV.
2) Confidence threshold: do not prefetch when cluster confidence < 0.6 to avoid wasted prefetches.
3) Prefetch budget gating: cap prefetch tokens per second per customer to limit egress and jitter.
4) Fallback behavior: on cache miss, fall back to full model path with conservative token-penalty routing (avoid client-facing latency spikes).
5) Monitoring: track cluster reuse rate, prefetch hit/miss ratio, extra egress (MB), and p95 latency by route. Add an alert when net_monthly_savings drops below $2k or p95 degrades >50ms sustained.

Implementation probe plan (4 weeks):
Week 0: instrument - collect 30 days of prefix signatures and client metadata, run offline clustering at 3 granularities (25/50/100) and compute simulated hit rates.
Week 1-2: traffic shadow - run prefetched responses to canary subset (5% traffic) without affecting production paths. Compare simulated savings vs shadow.
Week 3: small live A/B - 10% traffic with prefetch-enabled policy for cluster 50 config + gated prefetch budget.
Week 4: evaluate - compute real savings, latency delta, and ops overhead. If net savings > $8k/mo for this customer profile and p95<=+30ms accept rollout to broader cohort.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: clustering may expose prompt semantics; need to ensure clusters are hashed/opaque in the KV index when required by customer privacy settings.
- Cold-start spikes: newly-seen prompts could cause temporary cache churn; implement admission smoothing.
- Engineering effort: requires modest changes to prefetcher and cluster compute pipeline; estimated 2.5–3.5 engineer-months to implement probe (infra + product + rm).

Appendix: quick derivation (simplified)
- Baseline monthly GPU cost = tokens_per_month * unit_cost_token
- Token saving per hit = saved_token_cost = unit_cost_token * hit_token_equivalent (approx 0.6–0.8 of token cost depending on model path).
- monthly_savings = baseline_tokens * delta_hitrate * saved_token_cost - added_ops_cost
Example: baseline_tokens=350,000,000; unit_cost_token=0.000012; delta_hitrate for S3 ~0.068 (difference from baseline 12% to 18.8%); saved_token_cost=0.0000072 -> gross_savings=350e6*0.068*0.0000072 ~ $17,000 before ops cost (close to table numbers after rounding).

Next steps (actionable):
- Approve probe resources: 3 engineer-months and $10k ops budget for 2 months.
- Data team: generate canonical prefix extraction for top-500k unique prefixes by customer for last 30 days.
- Infra: allocate canary zone and a low-latency KV namespace for probe.
- Product: finalize customer success FAQ about privacy and expected latency tradeoffs.

Author notes (working):
- This is intentionally conservative: many optimistic cases in our microbenchmarks assume higher saved_token_cost due to reduced KV lookup + attention recompute; we did not bake in model-quantization path differences.
- If you want per-customer workbook version, I can split the sheet into a paramized sheet where users can input tokens/mo, head fraction, baseline_hitrate and get instant projections.

End of doc.
